title: Building a Compliant, Ethical Long-Term Business
originality: All items original to LicensePath. Modeled on the DRE exam blueprint and style only; no actual exam items reproduced.

questions.stem: A salesperson's best first step with an unfamiliar high-risk issue is to:
rationales: Improvisation can harm clients.
Correct. Broker supervision and qualified referral reduce risk.
An unsupported promise is risky.
Social media is not authority.

questions.stem: An AI tool removes a visible-stain reference from listing copy. The agent should:
options: Restore accurate information and use disclosure process
rationales: Publishing can mislead.
Correct. Tools do not remove disclosure duties.
AI output requires verification.
Concealment is improper.
Salespersons remain supervised.
Correct. The broker establishes oversight and procedures.
Title is a separate service.
Recording is a government function.

questions.stem: A client asks whether to waive every contingency. The agent should:
options: Explain the transaction purpose and route legal advice appropriately
Tell client contingencies do not matter
rationales: The decision belongs to the informed client.
Correct. The agent may explain process but should not give legal conclusions.
Acceptance cannot be guaranteed.
Contingencies can materially affect risk.

questions.stem: The safest rule for new client-facing technology is to:
options: Obtain required broker approval and protect client data
rationales: Unreviewed tools may create privacy and compliance risk.
Correct. Approved tools and secure handling protect clients.
Confidential files require approved handling.
Technology cannot replace qualified advice.

questions.stem: An inspector offers private referral payments. The agent should:
options: Bring it to broker and preserve client choice
rationales: Private arrangements can violate policy or law.
Correct. Referral arrangements require broker review and consumer choice.
Mandatory steering is improper.
The agent cannot guarantee a provider's work.

options: Preserved in the approved transaction record
rationales: Personal texts alone create a weak record.
Correct. Material instructions and decisions should be retained appropriately.
Closing does not erase record duties.
Public sharing may breach privacy.

questions.stem: The fairness question in an ethical decision test asks whether the agent would:
rationales: Correct. Consistency helps prevent discriminatory or favoritism-based conduct.
Commission is not the ethical standard.
Records are essential.
Client preference cannot authorize unlawful conduct.

questions.stem: A buyer asks for keys before closing. The agent should:
options: Confirm written authority, escrow status, and broker procedure
rationales: Informal access can create risk.
Correct. Possession requires authorized process.
The agent cannot promise it.
Verbal assurance may be inadequate.

questions.stem: A near miss should lead to:
options: Improving the process that allowed it
rationales: Hiding prevents learning.
Correct. Near misses reveal system weaknesses before harm occurs.
Blame does not improve a control.
Files should be retained under policy.

questions.stem: A friend says forms are unnecessary because they trust the agent. The agent should:
options: Use normal brokerage process and explain its protections
rationales: Friendship is not an exception.
Correct. Consistent process protects both client and agent.
Late paperwork may not cure omissions.
Authorized forms and supervision are required.

questions.stem: A suspected wire-fraud message should be handled by:
options: Independently verifying through a known contact
rationales: A fraudulent message can include a fraudulent number.
Correct. Known independent contact information is the control.
Unreviewed forwarding can spread harm.
Test funds can be stolen.

questions.stem: File audits are useful because they:
rationales: Communication remains necessary.
Correct. Audits reveal gaps while they may still be corrected.
Supervision remains necessary.
Audits are not legal advice.

questions.stem: A seller asks agent to hide a defect to protect price. The agent should:
rationales: Concealment is improper.
Correct. Material disclosure issues require accurate handling and broker involvement.
Buyer type does not eliminate duty.
Removing photos does not eliminate knowledge.

questions.stem: Which metric best supports a service-focused business?
rationales: Pressure can reward shortcuts.
Correct. Good metrics reinforce accurate, client-centered work.
More data is not necessarily better service.
Artificial urgency can harm consumers.

questions.stem: The strongest professional answer when facts are uncertain is:
options: A prompt, documented referral to the right expert
A promise to fix it personally
rationales: Guessing can mislead.
Correct. Appropriate escalation protects the client and preserves role boundaries.
Silence fails to serve the client.
The agent may lack authority or expertise.
